errors: No arithmetic errors in the main table; every quotient, refraction sum, latitude and weighted term was verified.
April 11, last column: the value must be +13.26 (= 26×0.51). The leading digit is overwritten or obscure; the sum only reproduces 49.42 with +13.26.

Sun coefficient 0.474: with φ = 51°31.8' and ε ≈ 23°28' the solstice zenith distance is ≈ 28°3', and sin = 0.470. 0.474 corresponds to z ≈ 28°18'. This is either a slight slip or a different assumed z (unsure). The tan z model fits worse (0.533), so sin z is the evident model.
The tabulated refraction values are roughly consistent with a constant ≈ 57–58" × tan z with pressure and temperature factors. They could not be recomputed exactly without Gauss's table.

results.what: Reduction of repeating-circle observations: mean zenith distance = (total arc + sum of meridian reductions)/n
results.modern_name: Repeating (Borda/Reichenbach) circle reduction with circum-meridian reduction

results.what: Latitude from lower culmination of Polaris, φ = 180° − z − δ
results.modern_name: Latitude by circumpolar star at lower transit

results.what: Weighted mean of latitudes with weights equal to number of repetitions, computed via deviations from 50''
Latitude sensitivity to a sin z-proportional zenith-distance error; opposite signs for north (Polaris) and south (Sun) objects, allowing elimination
results.modern_name: Flexure / systematic error elimination by north–south star combination

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observational reduction for the Göttingen latitude. The page itself is annotated as published in Werke VI, 396. Methods are standard practice of the period.

checkable.asserts: ≈ 0.6446: coefficient 0.645 is sin z at lower culmination
≈ 0.470: sin z of the Sun at summer solstice (compare written 0.474)

transcription_corrections: Column 6, first row: '27^z 8^l 2' is barometer 27 Zoll 8.2 Linien. Later entries (14.9, 13.3, 7.2, 9.3, 8.5, 10.9) are barometer readings, apparently Linien above 27 Zoll; column 7 is the thermometer.
April 11, last column: read '+13,26', not '+3,26' (overwritten digit).
April 11, declination seconds: '53,33' is confirmed by the latitude 50,51 (no [?] needed).
Header '51° 31' belongs to the latitude column; '88°19'' heads the declination column.
'49"42' below the table is the weighted mean latitude seconds.
Bottom-left 'Sin[?]' is an illegible struck word; 'aus' heads the list of observation types.
